I am assuming you mean The Bureau of Land Management. If you live in a western state with a lot of forestry, mining, and O&G development, you would understand why the BLM is a good thing to have. They make sure that areas are responsibly managed. The problem is a company can buy land that is cheap enough that they can extract 100% of the available resources, and not care about the long term management of the area. But in doing so, they ruin the land and negatively affect others. Logging is a prime example. Clear cutting thousands of contiguous acres at a time is profitable, but destroys all the ecosystems that support a healthy wildlife population. This means hunters can't go get elk, Polinators decline in number, soil gets blown away, erosion damages rivers hurting fish stocks, etc. Mining is also a good example of the issue. Miners extract the resources, filling lakes with heavy metals leaving open shafts and tailings piles that will never recover, then the company files for bankruptcy before cleaning it up, dissolves, and now the public is stuck with the mess.

The BLM can manage areas to get the most benefit for the public, whether that is allowing a company to responsibly use the area, or keeping it to support a healthy ecosystem.

AND, a national organization does not have the same budgetary concerns that state orgs do. This means that if O&G development slows, the state can't sell public lands to cover the downfall, and thus the area is preserved for the future.
